sections.h2: What should a Caldwell County seller know about the county first?
sections.html:
Caldwell County is a foothills county in the northwest of the state, formed in January 1841 from parts of Burke and Wilkes, with Lenoir as the county seat. The county's own history page places it about 69 miles northwest of Charlotte, with elevations running from 900 feet to 5,964 feet and the Yadkin, Johns and Catawba as its main rivers.

It has nine incorporated municipalities: Lenoir, Hudson, Granite Falls, Cedar Rock, Cajahs Mountain, Gamewell, Sawmills, and parts of Blowing Rock and Rhodhiss. The first modern furniture factories were organized here in 1889, and furniture work shows up repeatedly in local history. Which town a parcel falls in changes the bill, since each municipality adopts its own rate and a couple adopt none.

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 81,105, against 80,652 in the 2020 Census
  • Housing units on July 1, 2025: 38,057, with 73.5% owner-occupied for 2020-2024
  • Middle owner-occupied home value in the 2020-2024 figures: $192,200
  • Median gross rent: $744; median household income: $56,425
  • Residents 65 and older: 22.8%; land area 471.89 square miles; 501 building permits in 2025

sections.h2: Where is the Caldwell County Tax Office and what does it handle?
sections.html:
Find the Tax Office at 905 West Avenue NW, Lenoir, NC 28645. Visits work on weekdays between 8 and 5; the office shuts on weekends and federal holidays. The mailing address is PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645, and the main number in the county directory is 828-757-1340. Listing questions can also go to 828-757-1320.

The office lists personal property and business property, bills and collects the tax, and runs revaluation. For a home sale, the pieces that matter are the real estate value, the delinquent status of each year's bill and any relief program the owner is enrolled in. A tax lien on real property in the county is advertised by the county once bills go unpaid, and the commissioners authorized advertising of 2024 liens at their February 2025 meeting.

sections.h2: What is the payment deadline for Caldwell County property tax, and when does interest begin?
sections.html:
Bills come due on September 1. Interest begins on January 6 of the next year at 2 percent and climbs by three-fourths of a percent every month until the bill is settled. The tax office's FAQ adds that it judges timeliness by the postmark from the U.S. Postal Service and refuses postage-meter dates.

Some practical details from the same FAQ:

  • Partial payments are accepted from the time the bill arrives until January 6
  • Online payment accepts American Express, Discover, Mastercard, Visa or a PayPal account, and PayPal's processing fees are not kept by the county
  • An escrow account does not stop the bill from being mailed to you, so contact your lender if you think it should pay
  • Personal property bills such as boats and unlicensed vehicles are mailed in July

The 2026 rate chart also lists a discount of 2.00 for July and 1.00 for August. G.S. 105-360 lets a county adopt a prepayment discount schedule approved by the Department of Revenue, so ask the tax office how the discount is applied before relying on it.

sections.h2: What rates did Caldwell County list for 2026?
sections.html:
The 2026 chart lists 0.4666 for the county, and a town or district adds its own line. Counties quote these figures per $100 of assessed value. Lenoir shows 0.4600, with a separate special downtown district at 0.1800, and fire and rescue districts add further lines for rural parcels.

Before estimating a bill, ask the tax office which fire and rescue districts include your parcel.

sections.h2: What happened with the 2025 revaluation in Caldwell County?
sections.html:
Caldwell County reappraised all real property for 2025, after the county's sales-assessment ratio fell below the 0.85 threshold that triggers a reappraisal under state law. The county's own earlier revaluation took effect January 1, 2021, and the tax office's Q and A says the goal of a reappraisal is equal, uniform values for every taxpayer.

At a February 2025 commissioners' meeting the tax administrator said county staff appraised all residential property, and a third party handled commercial and industrial property. Around 450 appeals had been received at that point. Residents spoke about large jumps in assessed value at that meeting, and one commissioner said the board would cut the rate as far as it could toward revenue neutral. That record shows why an owner who sells should check the assessed value on the bill before comparing it with an offer.

State law sets an eight-year outer limit under G.S. 105-286, yet a county of 75,000 residents or more must move up its reappraisal if the sales ratio slips under .85 or climbs over 1.15. Caldwell County's 2025 reappraisal followed that trigger, so owners should check their parcel's value on the bill.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Caldwell County property value?
sections.html:
File for an informal review first, because the Board of Equalization and Review only picks up the case afterward. Under the county's revaluation Q and A, an owner who disagrees returns an Informal Review Form, and the best evidence is a recent fee appraisal backed by local sales or a comparison of similar homes by year built, size, construction and acreage. The county advises against paying for an independent appraisal unless you feel it is truly needed.

The Board of Equalization and Review is the formal appeals board, and appeals from it go to the NC Property Tax Commission. Under G.S. 105-322, the board convenes for the first time between early April and early May, and your hearing request has to reach it before adjournment. The commissioners' policy sets the Caldwell board at five members and four alternates, who must have lived in the county at least two years.

Personal property is separate: appeals of individual or business personal property values must be in writing to the Caldwell County Assessor's Office, PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645, within 30 days of the tax bill date. Business listings that miss the January 31 deadline without an approved extension carry a 10 percent penalty on the total tax.

sections.h2: What relief and special programs apply to Caldwell County homeowners?
sections.html:
Caldwell County follows the state's three programs, and the county tax site provides a relief brochure and an application. The elderly or disabled exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1 shelters the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of a residence's appraised value, and the state's 2026 form sets the income cap at $38,800.

The disabled veteran exclusion takes the first $45,000 of appraised value, and the circuit breaker caps tax at 4.0 or 5.0 percent of income, with the 2026 upper threshold printed as $58,200. Form AV-9 is the application, filed with the county assessor, and June 1 before the tax year is the last day the county must accept it. Owners cannot stack the three programs.

If you list real estate improvements, the county says to report new buildings and additions during January with your cost and the percent complete on January 1, and to report demolished improvements as well.

sections.h2: Who owes the Caldwell County tax bill when a house is sold?
sections.html:
Caldwell County bills the January 1 owner; a seller who closed later should hand the bill to the buyer. The lien attaches as of January 1 under G.S. 105-355, the closing attorney should settle the current year and any open prior years.

Ask the Tax Office for a written payoff and check the town or fire district on the bill, since the combined charge varies by parcel. If the house was inherited or has back years unpaid, get the full list of open years before you accept an offer, since delinquent taxes are collected through foreclosure.

faqs.q: When are Caldwell County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1 of the tax year. Interest begins January 6 of the following year at 2 percent, then three-fourths of one percent a month until paid, and the county uses the U.S. Postal postmark, not a meter date.

faqs.q: Where do I pay or ask about my Caldwell County tax bill?
faqs.a: Visit 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir on a weekday between 8 and 5, or call 828-757-1340. Online payment works by credit card or PayPal, and the processing fees go to PayPal rather than the county.

faqs.q: When did Caldwell County last revalue property?
faqs.a: The county reappraised real property for 2025, and before that the county's revaluation took effect on January 1, 2021. State law requires a reappraisal at least every eight years, and sooner when the sales ratio falls below .85.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Caldwell County real estate value?
faqs.a: Return the informal review form with comparable sales or an appraisal. If the answer disappoints you, ask the Board of Equalization and Review for a hearing ahead of its adjournment. Appeals from the board go to the NC Property Tax Commission within 30 days of its mailed decision.

faqs.q: If I sold my Caldwell County house after January 1, who gets the bill?
faqs.a: Billing follows the January 1 owner, so send a copy to the buyer. The county says it tries to notify the new owner but asks sellers to help.
